I'll admit upfront that I don't know all the details about how the program as a whole is going, but from what I've gathered over the last few years it doesn't look pretty. What I have come to believe is that there will soon be a point that too many people are receiving payments from it than are going into it. There aren't enough younger people making enough money to offset the older people that need the money. So here are my thoughts on it.

I get that we can't just cut it off next year, people have been paying in to the system their whole lives and expect to get something out. Doubly so if they are nearing the time when they can begin receiving payments. But I still feel like it has to stop somewhere, someone is going to have to pay the bill without getting the benefits. I've been vocal in person about this but not adamant that it is the only way, just my perception of a painful truth. Which is why I'd be willing to pay into the system for the rest of my life and forfeit my right to withdraw from it later in life if it means we can gently end it without impacting my children's future in a drastic way. I understand the base reasoning for many government safety nets, but I don't like the idea that my kids are going to have to pay for me to survive later. I want to be able to not only support myself until the day I die, but also leave a little extra for them when that time comes. I want to pay for my own funeral, pick out my own casket, my own gravestone, etc. I just want my kids to show up, cry, laugh, and be happy. I hate thinking what kind of nonsense they'll be putting up with if the government continues down the path of absurdity that it has been over the last decade.

Which is why I'd like to get your thoughts on realistic ways to either fix the program or end it gracefully. I fall into the camp that believes it isn't sustainable so it needs to end.
